# negotiation_email-examples dataset

Internal dataset of an AI assistant drafting negotiation emails and messages.

- Data lives in `data/entries.dat` (one JSON object per line, fields: `prompt`, `response`).
- Add entries ONE AT A TIME with the CLI (direct edits to the data file will fail the
  integrity check and be rejected in review):

      echo '{"prompt": "...", "response": "..."}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py

- Before pushing, run `make check`.
</tool_response>

{"prompt": "I got a job offer for $95k but I was hoping for $110k. Help me write a counter-offer email.", "response": "Subject: Re: Offer for Senior Analyst — A Quick Follow-Up

Hi Priya,

Thank you again for the offer — I'm genuinely excited about the role and the team. Before I confirm, I wanted to discuss the compensation package.

Based on my research into market rates for this role and my six years of relevant experience in forecasting, I was hoping we could land closer to $110,000 base. I'm confident I can bring a lot of value from day one, and I'd love to find a number that works well for both sides.

Happy to hop on a call this week if that's easier.

Best,
Jordan"}
{"prompt": "Draft an email asking my landlord to reduce the rent increase from 12% to something more reasonable.", "response": "Subject: Regarding the Proposed Rent Increase

Hi Teresa,

Thank you for the renewal notice. I've valued being a reliable tenant here for three years and would like to continue, but a 12% increase is a significant jump above what I've seen for comparable units in the area (closer to 4-6%).

Would you be open to meeting somewhere in that range instead? I'm glad to sign a longer lease term if that helps make a smaller increase workable on your end.

I appreciate you considering this, and I'm happy to discuss further whenever works for you.

Best regards,
Alex"}
{"prompt": "I need to tell a client their project will be delayed by two weeks without losing their trust.", "response": "Subject: Project Timeline Update

Hi Renata,

I want to flag an update on our timeline as early as possible. We've hit an unexpected integration issue with the payments provider that will push our delivery date back by two weeks, to the 24th.

We're already adding an extra QA pass and reallocating a second engineer to prevent further slippage, and I'll send a short progress update next Monday so you're not waiting in the dark. I know timing matters on your end, and I take that seriously — happy to discuss any ways we can soften the impact on your side.

Thanks for your patience on this.

Sam"}
</tool_response>

5. Countering a purchase offer on a used item

We really like the platform and the features you outlined fit our needs well.\n\nThat said, our budget for this category this year sits at around $18,000 for the annual license. I know that is below your quoted price, so I wanted to reach out directly to see if there is any flexibility — perhaps by adjusting the user count, extending the commitment to 24 months, or bundling with a reduced onboarding fee.\n\nWe are keen to move forward and would prefer to do so with your team. Is there room to bridge the gap?\n\nBest,\nDiana"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py

echo '{"prompt": "Help me write a message to my manager asking for more flexible hours because of my childcare schedule.", "response": "Subject: Quick Note on My Work Hours

Hi Tom,

I wanted to bring up something that would really help me stay productive and balanced. With my youngest just starting preschool, I have a bit of a window each morning that makes an 8:30 start difficult on some days.

Would you be open to me shifting my hours slightly — say 9:15 to 6:15 — or working from home on Tuesdays and Thursdays when the morning drop-off runs later? My core overlap with the team would remain fully covered, and I will make sure to keep all meetings and deliverables on track.

I am happy to trial this for a month and check in to see if it works for the team. Let me know what you think.

Thanks,
Rachel"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>

echo '{"prompt": "Draft a counter-offer message for a freelance client who wants to reduce my rate from $85/hr to $70/hr.", "response": "Hi Ben,

Thanks for the note and for continuing to work with us on the campaign. I appreciate you sharing the budget constraints upfront.

Regarding the rate, $70/hr is a bit below what I currently charge, and I have been maintaining $85 to cover the scope of strategy plus execution that we discuss. That said, I value our relationship and would like to find a way to make this work.

One option would be to lock in $80/hr if we can agree on a standing monthly retainer of at least 20 hours — that gives you some savings and gives me more visibility into workload. If the project scope can be narrowed (for example, removing the competitor analysis component), I could also meet you closer to $75.

Does either of those approaches work for you? Happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Priya"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
OK: entry added

echo '{"prompt": "Write an email to a supplier explaining that their delivery was 5 days late and requesting a discount on the next order.", "response": "Subject: Late Delivery — Order #4472

Hi Kevin,

I wanted to flag that our last order (#4472) arrived five days after the agreed delivery date. This put us in a tight spot because we had to expedite a secondary supplier to keep our production line running, and it disrupted our schedule for the week.

We have been a reliable customer for the past 18 months and always pay within the 15-day window, so I wanted to bring this to you directly before escalating internally. Going forward, we need deliveries to arrive on the committed date.

As a gesture of goodwill, could you apply a 5% discount to our next purchase order? That would help offset the extra costs we incurred and would go a long way toward maintaining the partnership on good terms.

I look forward to hearing your thoughts.

Regards,
Miguel"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

<tool_response>
OK: entry added

<parameter=command>
echo '{"prompt": "I need to negotiate a partnership where a marketing agency wants 30% of ad revenue, but I want to offer them 15% plus a fixed monthly fee instead.", "response": "Subject: Partnership Terms — Proposal for Adjustment

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for putting together the initial partnership framework. We are excited about the potential of combining your ad network reach with our content platform.

On the revenue split, we have modeled the volumes and feel that a flat 30% would make it difficult for us to maintain the content quality that ultimately drives user engagement and, by extension, your ad revenue. Instead, would you consider a structure of 15% of ad revenue plus a fixed monthly retainer of $4,000? That way you have guaranteed income while we retain more of the upside from content growth.

We believe this aligns our incentives better and reflects the production costs on our side. Open to discussing the numbers if you would like to see the model we ran.

Best regards,
Ethan"}' | python3 scripts/add_entry.py
</parameter>
</function>

Done. I've successfully extended the dataset with 5 original, varied negotiation email entries:

1. **Vendor pricing negotiation** — Countering a $24k software license quote with a $18k budget, suggesting alternatives like longer commitments or reduced onboarding fees.
2. **Flexible work hours request** — Asking a manager for adjusted hours due to childcare, proposing a trial period.
3. **Freelance rate counter-offer** — Responding to a client who wants to reduce a rate from $85/hr to $70/hr, offering retainer-based alternatives.
4. **Late delivery complaint with discount request** — Addressing a 5-day late shipment and asking for a 5% discount on the next order.
5. **Partnership revenue split negotiation** — Proposing a restructured deal (15% rev share + fixed fee) instead of the agency's 30% revenue share demand.

`make check` confirms all 8 entries pass integrity validation.

final_entries.prompt: I want to negotiate with a software vendor who quoted $24,000 for their enterprise license. My budget is $18,000. Draft an email to open the negotiation.

Subject: Enterprise License — Pricing Discussion

Hi Marcus,

Thanks for sending over the proposal. We really like the platform and the features you outlined fit our needs well.

That said, our budget for this category this year sits at around $18,000 for the annual license. We are keen to move forward and would prefer to do so with your team. Is there room to bridge the gap?

Best,
Diana
